commits.author: Boris
commits.subject: fix(cron): list-crons merges cron-state.json into Last Fire display
commits.body:
list-crons read crons.json only and showed - in the Last Fire column
even when the daemon had recorded fires in cron-state.json. Confirmed
on nick: cron-state.json had heartbeat last_fire 20:32 UTC, CLI showed -.

Daemon writes fires to two surfaces:
- crons.json.last_fired_at via cron-scheduler.updateCron()
- cron-state.json.last_fire via bus update-cron-fire (called by skills)

Take max(crons.json.last_fired_at, cron-state.json.last_fire) per cron
for both the table display and the next-fire calculation, so users see
the true most-recent fire regardless of which path recorded it.

commits.author: Boris
commits.subject: fix(cron): scheduler catch-up reads cron-state.json
commits.body:
loadCrons() computed referenceMs from def.last_fired_at (crons.json)
only. For crons that pre-date the external-cron migration, last_fire
lives in cron-state.json (written by bus update-cron-fire from agent
skills) and crons.json.last_fired_at is empty. Result: scheduler
computed referenceMs=now and skipped catch-up, silently dropping
overdue fires (e.g. boris.heartbeat last fired 16:49 UTC stayed
unfired post-restart at 23:02 UTC despite being overdue).

Take Math.max(crons.json.last_fired_at, cron-state.json.last_fire)
per cron. Resolve stateDir from CTX_ROOT (not homedir) so test
sandboxes don't bleed production state.

commits.author: Boris
commits.subject: fix(cron): defer reload for in-flight fires to prevent double-fire race
commits.body:
When `bus update-cron` (or add/remove-cron) signals a daemon reload while
a tick's onFire is awaiting, the captured ScheduledCron reference becomes
orphaned: the new map holds a freshly-built entry that defaults
firing=false and computes nextFireAt from the stale crons.json
last_fired_at (the in-flight fire's persist hasn't run yet). On the next
tick, the new entry catch-up-fires the same logical event a second time.

Fix: when reload encounters an entry that is currently firing
(existing.firing === true), preserve the existing ScheduledCron as-is.
The new schedule applies on the next reload after the fire completes —
either the natural post-fire tick boundary or a subsequent IPC signal.

Test reproduces the race with a slow onFire interleaved between reload
and resolve. Pre-fix: slowFire called 2x. Post-fix: called 1x.

Found during multi-agent end-to-end verification of BUG 5 catch-up loop.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Boris
commits.subject: fix(cron): lazy-create scheduler when reload hits start-window gap
commits.body:
reloadCrons() previously returned true for any registered agent even when no
scheduler existed in cronSchedulers. This silently dropped reload requests
during the start-window gap between this.agents.set(name, ...) (line 271) and
startAgentCronScheduler(name) (line 288), across the await agentProcess.start()
yield in startAgent.

A `bus add-cron` IPC landing in that window would write crons.json, ask the
daemon to reload, get true back, and the cron would never fire until the next
daemon boot.

Fix: lazy-wire the scheduler when missing for non-Hermes agents so the
just-written crons.json is read immediately. Hermes agents intentionally have
no daemon scheduler (they manage crons natively), so for them the reload
remains a no-op that returns true.

Adds 4 tests in agent-manager.test.ts covering the lazy-create path, the
Hermes no-op, scheduler reuse, and the agent-not-running case.

commits.author: Boris
commits.subject: fix(cron): distinguish legitimately-empty from corrupt in lastGoodSchedule fallback
commits.body:
iter 9 — empty-result fallback regression in cron-scheduler.loadCrons.

The previous fallback gated only on `nextScheduled.size === 0 &&
lastGoodSchedule.size > 0`, which could not tell "user removed the last
cron" (legitimate empty) from "file unparseable" (corruption). Result:
removing the last cron via `bus remove-cron` restored it from
lastGoodSchedule and kept firing it until daemon restart or another
non-empty reload.

Fix (option B from the iter 8 audit handoff):

- Add `readCronsWithStatus(): { crons, corrupt }` to src/bus/crons.ts.
  `corrupt: true` only when the primary file is unparseable AND the
  .bak fallback also failed/missing. A clean parse to `[]`, or a missing
  file, both report `corrupt: false`.

- cron-scheduler.loadCrons now calls readCronsWithStatus and gates the
  lastGoodSchedule fallback on `corrupt === true`. Legitimate empties
  clear the schedule as the user expects.

- readCrons keeps its existing signature (delegates to the new function)
  so the 8 existing callers stay untouched.

Tests:
- tests/unit/daemon/cron-scheduler.test.ts: replace iter 8 it.todo with
  a real "remove-cron of LAST cron clears schedule" assertion. Add a
  paired "corrupt:true retains last-good schedule" test to pin the
  surviving corruption path.
- tests/unit/bus/crons-io.test.ts: 5 new tests directly exercising
  readCronsWithStatus across the missing/empty/.bak-recovered/both-
  corrupt/no-bak axes.
- tests/integration/phase5-audit.test.ts: existing AD-4 test was
  unintentionally exercising the bug (it wrote a valid empty crons
  array and expected lastGoodSchedule to engage). Updated to corrupt
  both files so it actually tests the corruption path it claims to.

Suite: 1435 passing | 1 skipped | 0 failing | 0 todo (was 1430 + 1 todo).

commits.author: Boris
commits.subject: test(cron): pin iter 10 daemon-crash mid-fire double-fire (iter 11 fix flagged)
commits.body:
Audit-only commit (mirrors iter 8 pattern). Adds a passing test that pins
the current double-fire behavior when the daemon crashes between
sc.firing=true and the post-success updateCron persist call. On restart,
crons.json.last_fired_at is still the pre-fire value, so loadCrons's
catch-up gate fires the same logical tick again — two prompt injections
for one scheduled window.

sc.firing is in-memory only and the reload-while-firing guard at line 377
only protects IPC reloads, not process-level crashes.

Iter 11 fix candidate (placed inline as it.todo): persist
last_fire_attempted_at to crons.json BEFORE awaiting onFire and include
it in loadCrons's referenceMs candidates. Crash mid-fire → restart sees
attempted_at = now → no catch-up.
